resources.string: EchoCatch is built to notice when someone calls your name while you wear earphones, and then lower or pause your music so you can hear.
The phone\'s microphone, but only while you switch Listening on.
It is analysed on this phone and thrown away. Nothing is recorded or saved, and nothing is sent anywhere: the app has no internet access at all.
Android shows a notification the whole time the microphone is open, with a Stop button.
This early version only checks that the microphone and the background service work. It does not detect your name yet.
Next, Android will ask whether EchoCatch may use the microphone. Choose \"While using the app\" (or \"Allow\"). The microphone is only used while Listening is on.
Android is not showing the question any more, so it has to be switched on in the app settings: open Permissions, then Microphone, then choose Allow. Come back here afterwards.

While the microphone is open, Android requires a notification. Allowing notifications keeps it visible, with a Stop button. Without it, listening still works, but you could miss that the microphone is on.
Whose name should it listen for?
Type it the way you would write it. It stays on this phone.
For names that are spelled differently from how they sound, for example \"Shivawn\" for Siobhan.
Use letters, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens and full stops only.
Keep each entry to 40 characters or fewer.
Tap Start to open the microphone.
The microphone is open. Tap Stop, or use the notification, to close it.
The microphone is open but only silence is arriving. Another app may be using it, or the phone has muted it.
This version is a first step
It checks that the microphone and the background service work. It does not detect your name yet and will not pause your music.
Tip: keep EchoCatch in recent apps. On some phones, swiping it away stops listening. Settings explains how to prevent that.
Notifications are off for EchoCatch, so the listening notification may be hidden. Turn them on in Settings to see it and its Stop button.
Listening stopped because EchoCatch does not have the microphone permission.
Listening stopped because the microphone could not be opened. Another app or a phone call may be using it.
Listening stopped because the microphone stopped delivering sound.
Android did not let EchoCatch start listening in the background. Open the app and tap Start.
Listening was ended by Android. Phones often do this when the app is swiped away from recent apps, or after a restart. Tap Start to resume.

Some phones stop an app when it is swiped away from recent apps, and its notification disappears with it. If yours does: first, lock EchoCatch in recent apps (long-press or pull down its card, then choose Lock; the wording differs between phones). Second, in the app\'s battery settings, allow background activity. EchoCatch does not ask Android to ignore battery optimisation.
Sound from the microphone is analysed on this phone and discarded. Nothing is recorded, saved or sent anywhere. The app has no internet permission.
Shown while the microphone is open.
Tells you when listening ended without you stopping it.
The microphone is open. This version does not detect your name yet.
